I gave it a try, but the gameplay and overall experience didn't click with me, and I didn't find myself enjoying it the way I expected to. I can understand why so many cozy gamers love it, but it simply didn't resonate with my personal taste.

Just not my kind of game

I tried A Short Hike because of its overwhelming positive ratings, even though it didn’t really look like my type of game. Turns out, it isn’t.

I appreciate the 3D pixel-art style, and the movement feels smooth. Gliding around is genuinely well done. But I’m not a fan of fetch-style exploration games, and my sense of direction doesn’t mesh well with them.

I can see why others enjoy it, but I review based on whether I’d recommend it to someone like me, and I wouldn’t. I even had my wife try it, and she didn’t enjoy it either.

In principle, the game is really nice, calm, and relaxing. Had it stuck to its core premise (a short hike), it would have been a truly great, albeit short, experience.

However, for some unclear reason, someone decided to add some collectathon features. The game has really terrible orientation - there is no map, only a compass, but your view gets regularly turned around, so "north" can be in every direction. This feature is already annoying enough in the core game, but when it comes to searching for every possible nook and cranny, the location finding is utterly frustrating. Setting aside the point that there is no point to the collections at all (yes, all collectathons are somewhat pointless), finding all collectibles takes about as long as finishing the game. Unfortunately, this is also about the time that it takes to leave me annoyed, and frustrated, so that the final impression is really bad.

The Good:
I liked climbing and flying and swimming and helping various people around the island. I liked the feeling of getting to the top of the mountain. I liked finding treasure chests and coins on the ground.
The Bad:
I did not like how monotonous it felt. Find feather, climb a little higher. Talk to two people who have very little depth, find another feather. The first time I played this, I speed ran getting to the top of the mountain. The second time, I wanted to try and help everyone and get some more achievements. I never finished the second play. Personally, I think it's boring and too difficult considering how fast it is to finish. 
The Ugly?:
I couldn't see this game having a different art style, but I still don't like it. It's cute, don't get me wrong, but the camera angles mixed with the lack of depth perception mixed with hardly being able to see a four-pixel object you need to be able to progress makes for a difficult time.
I would recommend this game to people who want something quick and simple.

reviews.review: GIVE ME A DAMN MAP, I GET LOST ALL THE TIME!

The game itself is pretty solid, collect feathers and bits, explore more, collect more bits, but it's buried underneath this layer of Hope Punk twee garbage writing that makes interacting with it feel vaguely shameful. If you are someone who unironically refers to dogs as hecking puppers or big chungus you'll probably be fine with it but every time someone opened their mouth in game my skin crawled.
The game features a healing art style and lighthearted plot. But it lacks a mini - map and has almost no quest guidance. Without a guide, it's hard to imagine many people completing it.

The game and music definitely give off a cozy vibe, but the overall experience feels way TOO short for me. You can probably finish the whole thing in about 30–45 minutes. I know it's called "short" hike, but 30 minutes to finish the game and i'm not even rushing. There are plenty of other chill, relaxing games out there that offer more playtime for the same—or even lower—price.

Don’t believe anyone who says the story is a masterpiece or peak writing, lol. You could sum up the entire plot of your character hiking up a mountain in less than 3 sentences (and I’m being really generous here). Most of the side quests and fetch tasks felt pretty boring to me. You’re mostly just walking around collecting stuff, and the game doesn't give you much motivation or a meaningful reason to do it.

If you enjoy games where you just walk around, soak in some nice pixel art, and don’t mind spending a few bucks on a 30 - 60 minute game with a barebones story and side quests that feel like a grocery list, then this might be for you.

Personally, I didn’t feel the game full price was justified by what the game delivered

The whole thing feels like it lacks meaningfulness—kinda like a Godard movie, less the accidental moments of zest that make it actually interesting to watch. Seriously, I have to hike a mountain to just make a phone call making some tedious small talk as I go? Doesn't feel like you do anything much; more like watching everything pass by, just sitting there, and occasionally meowing out your presence to others. The game does have a cozy vibe to it and the graphics are soothing, but other than that it's so uneventful chugging a glass of water with a cockroach feels less underwhelming

Probably, not my thing simply. Still, might be perfectly fine for the people who gawk at a progress bar loading and think, "Ah yes. Now this is living."

Overall: 5.769/10 wistful sighs into the void,
6/10 square feet of watching lead paint dry

This game is a slog fest and two of the achievements are completing ridiculous mini-games which blow away the "relaxing atmosphere" this game is promoted to have and they really have nothing to with "hiking" or exploration.  One of those mini games, which is a boat race to be completed in under 45 seconds, the dev decided to add insult to injury by adding 10 seconds to the total time every time the boat hit something otherwise I might have had it except I hit something heading for the finish, ffs!.  The dev said players should practice the run a bit to get used to it.  Really?  Like I have said before, if I wanted to boat race I would buy a boat racing game.  I did not purchase a boat racing game but a "hike through peaceful mountainside landscapes", an exploration game.  Maybe the achievement should have been when players played well enough to get the gold feather, which I am sure most of them did, and not something ridiculously harder to ruin any fun being had in this game,  The camera angles are at odds with the player and turn at the most inconvenient times, like when you are flying, about to finish/win a race etc. (which btw it didn't do when getting to the top of the mountain without the race - go figure).  There is not an in game map and finding places is tedious and time consuming even though I thought I knew where they were because I passed them so many times.  The only thing this game has going for it is that you can glide/fly like you were able to in "Firefall" (maybe better), although it doesn't look as pretty (gliding or scenery). This could have been an okay game with out the BS achievements but it is not really worth playing when there are better games out there that respect the player.

After hearing high praise from Dunkey, I kind of expected a little bit more. At it's price point maybe a little expensive, and while the writing can be both funny and heartfelt, there really isn't that much of it. Which leaves you with the actual game: it is very exploratory, enjoyable to run around in, and it is satisfying to gather what you need to climb the summit, but also a bit clunky: super easy to get lost on the island once you get far enough from the initial linear path, and gathering money is a bit of a pain. I'd suggest passing unless you REALLY like atmospheric games.

A very slight walking simulator that gets by on aesthetic. Pretty easily finished in 90 minutes, it is tough to recommend this, especially at full price of $8. There's nothing especially bad here. You walk, climb, and fly around the island. When you tire of doing grindy collecathons you can head to the peak. The biggest difficulty is the camera which is fixed in position and made it way harder than it needed to be to figure out where I was and where I needed to be going.

The pretty seamless addition of a third dimension via climbing, gliding, and very slight amounts of flying is a nice change to the usual mostly two-dimensional world (since humans can't fly) you get in games. Everything is chill and cosy but....there's no real story here. You're walking around and soaking in the vibes for an hour or two.

I actually very much prefer these kind of short, targeted, single-player experiences. I rarely play games that take more than 10-12 hours to complete. But this goes too far in the other direction, especially in the absence of any story, puzzles, or compelling game mechanics.

I feel silly saying this about a game called "a short hike", but it's like... really short. I like exploration and it's fun to check every nook and cranny of the island for collectibles (like hats!). The dialogue is witty and it's got a serene atmosphere. It would have been great if it hadn't been over in just two hours (and that's including several side quests I took). The gimmicks which are meant to extend gameplay (like completing the fish book) just aren't innovative or engaging enough to make me feel they're worth the trouble. Maybe they could have added caves to explore. A map would have been nice too.

I wanted to love this game so much, because of all of the positive reviews.....but.....unfortunately it is not the game for me. I felt like I would be just going in circles not sure if I was going the right direction since you can only see a limited area.  This game unfortunately at the end of the day, made me feel stupid, when I am far from that.  I am glad everyone else is enjoying the game :)
